items.title: Follow-up from "fix(auth): prevent stale config writes from clobbering rotated OAuth tokens"
items.body:
The following discussion from !3501 should be addressed:

- [ ] @phikai started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3501#note_3553777507):  (+1 comment)

    > Consider moving this helper next to `unmarshal`/`marshal` in [`internal/oauth2/config.go`](internal/oauth2/config.go) as `MergeFresherCredentialsFromDisk(cfg, dir)` and calling it from `Write()` via a small hook. The logic is OAuth-specific (three named keys, expiry-date semantics, single-use refresh token) — the generic `config` package doesn't otherwise know about OAuth, and this is the layer that'd be extended if another single-use rotating credential ever showed up.
    > 
    > Not a blocker if you'd rather keep it here for now, but call it out as a followup.

items.title: lint CI job is non-deterministic: nolintlint flags different pre-existing directives across retries
items.body:
## Problem

The `lint` CI job (golangci-lint via `gitlab.com:443/gitlab-org/dependency_proxy/containers/golangci/golangci-lint:v2.13.1-alpine`) intermittently fails `nolintlint` on pre-existing `//nolint:staticcheck` directives that are unrelated to the changes in the triggering MR, and the specific set of flagged lines changes between retries of the same commit.

## Evidence

Observed on !3955 (`fix(iostreams): make background/color detection reachable, add --color mode`), which touches only `internal/iostreams/`, `internal/theme/`, `internal/commands/help/`, `internal/commands/root.go`, `internal/config/schema.go`, and `cmd/glab/main.go` — none of the flagged files below.

Run 1 (job 16669762994):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/issue/create/issue_create.go:164:41
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
```

Run 2, a retry of the same commit (job 16698765802):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
internal/commands/mr/view/mr_view.go:278:50          <- different from run 1
```

Run 3, another retry of the same commit (job 16698812448):
```
internal/commands/ci/cancel/job/job.go:117:5
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:596:30
internal/commands/issue/board/view/issue_board_view.go:597:39
internal/commands/issue/create/issue_create.go:164:41   <- back to run 1's set
internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_publish.go:164:2
```

Three of the five lines are stable across all three runs (`job.go:117`, `issue_board_view.go:596` and `:597`, `mr_note_publish.go:164`); the fifth line alternates between `issue_create.go:164` and `mr_view.go:278`. All five commits are identical (same SHA, same merge ref) — only the job run differs.

Control: `main`'s own scheduled/push pipelines (e.g. 2877065714, 2873335961, 2871184860) are all green, so this isn't a straightforward "these nolint comments are stale" finding — if it were, `main` would fail identically and deterministically every time.

## Hypothesis (unconfirmed — MEASURED vs UNPROVEN)

**UNPROVEN:** `nolintlint`'s "is this directive unused" check depends on `staticcheck` having actually run its own analysis at that location within the same invocation. If golangci-lint analyzes packages concurrently with a bounded worker pool, and `staticcheck`'s SA1019 (deprecated-symbol) analysis has some cross-package or cache-sharing state, a race in which packages have completed analysis by the time `nolintlint` evaluates a given file could explain why the flagged set varies between runs of the same commit. This needs someone who's traced golangci-lint's own concurrency model to confirm — I haven't done that here.

**MEASURED:** the failing line set differs across 3 runs of the identical commit; `main`'s pipelines are consistently green; none of the flagged files are touched by the triggering MR's diff.

## Impact

Any MR can hit this regardless of what it touches, and a maintainer retrying the job has roughly even odds of getting a different failure rather than a pass, based on this sample. Worth investigating before it becomes a routine "just retry lint" tax on every MR.

## Suggested next step

Someone with context on `!3920`'s (CI parallelization) cache-key work or golangci-lint's concurrency settings for this project should look at whether `nolintlint` + `staticcheck` need `GOMAXPROCS=1` or a `run.concurrency: 1` setting in `.golangci.yml`, or whether this is a known upstream golangci-lint issue with a version fix available.

items.title: `host` config key / GITLAB_HOST overrides repo remotes instead of acting as a fallback
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)
  - Also reproduced from source at main (`glab DEV`)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _both_
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) _v19.3.3_
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

The top-level `host:` key in `config.yml` (or the `GITLAB_HOST` / `GITLAB_URI` / `GL_HOST` environment variables) is treated as an **override when inside a Git repository** instead of as a default for when no host can be resolved. When the key differs from the repo's remote host, glab filters the remotes down to the configured host and fails all repo-bound commands. The key is documented as "Default GitLab instance, outside Git repositories", so it should only apply when the remote (or a URL argument) doesn't determine the host.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)

### Steps to reproduce

With no network required (the failure happens before any API call):

```sh
git init /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
git remote add origin https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git
mkdir -p /tmp/cfg && cat > /tmp/cfg/config.yml <<'EOF'
git_protocol: https
host: gitlab.tuwien.ac.at
hosts:
  gitlab.tuwien.ac.at:
    token: fake
    api_protocol: https
    git_protocol: https
EOF
chmod 600 /tmp/cfg/config.yml
GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg glab issue list
```

Setting `host:` to anything other than `gitlab.com` (or setting `GITLAB_HOST`) triggers the filter in any repo whose remote points to a different instance.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

1. The command fails with `None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable` even when **no** environment variable is set and the value came from the `host:` key — the error message is misleading.
2. With `-R OWNER/REPO` (no host in the argument), the request silently goes to the configured instance instead of the repo's remote host, targeting the wrong instance and token.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

- Inside a Git repository, the remote (or a URL argument) determines the host; the `host:` key / `GITLAB_HOST` are only fallbacks when the host cannot be resolved (e.g. outside a repo).
- The error message should say which source set the override (config key vs. env var).

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

```
$ GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg GLAB_DEBUG=true glab issue list
2026/10/08 19:04:51 [Could not determine base repo in telemetry hook:  none of the git remotes
configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable. Try adding
a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

Configured remotes: gitlab.com]

   ERROR

  None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST
  environment variable. Try adding a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

  GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

  Configured remotes: gitlab.com.
```

(Note: in the debug log line, the trailing `]` closes the `GLAB_DEBUG` log entry, which wraps the message in brackets; it is not part of the error text.)

### Possible fixes

- `internal/cmdutils/factory.go`: `defaultHostname` is set from `cfg.Get("", "host")` before `BaseRepo()` resolves; `Remotes()` then sets `hostOverride` whenever the default differs from `gitlab.com` (\~line 192).
- `internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go`: the `hostOverride` block (\~lines 103-127) drops all non-matching remotes, then errors out.
- `RepoOverride` (`factory.go`) resolves `-R OWNER/REPO` against `defaultHostname` instead of the repo's remote host.
- Note: `remote_resolver_test.go` (\~line 428) locks in the current override behavior, so this needs a decision on intended semantics (env var as hard override vs. fallback), not just a test change.
- Related: #8084 covers the URL-host case of the same host-resolution model.
